zh.title: 塞斯納441包機於阿拉斯加軍用雷達站附近墜毀 機上8人全數罹難
zh.summary: 塞斯納包機於阿拉斯加雷達站附近墜毀；機上8人全數罹難；運安會已展開調查
body: 一架載有8人的塞斯納441 Conquest II（Cessna 441 Conquest II）雙引擎渦輪螺旋槳包機，於當地時間2026年8月20日約12時15分，在美國阿拉斯加州西部紐恩漢角長程雷達站機場（EHM）（Cape Newenham Long Range Radar Site Airport）以西的陸地上墜毀。美國聯邦航空總署（FAA）證實該起事故，救援人員接報抵達現場後，確認機上8人全數罹難，無人生還。
根據官方資訊，該架失事客機註冊編號為N128EZ，製造年份為1979年，由總部位於安克拉治的安克拉治安全航空（Security Aviation）負責營運。該班機當天自泰德·史蒂文斯安克拉治國際機場（ANC）起飛，機上載有2名飛行員及6名乘客。美國陸軍工兵署（US Army Corps of Engineers）隨後證實該班機為其承租，且罹難者中有2名為該署員工。
事故發生的紐恩漢角長程雷達站機場位於安克拉治以西約450英里處，為美國空軍所屬的私人飛行場，由太平洋空軍區域支援中心管理，專門提供給監視阿拉斯加及周邊領空防務的雷達站使用。該機場設有一條長約3,945英尺、寬150英尺的15/33碎石跑道，跑道位於山坡之上，且兩端高差超過300英尺。
國家運輸安全委員會（NTSB）阿拉斯加辦公室主管指出，該客機是在準備進場降落時發生墜毀。聯邦航空總署的機場資料警告，該跑道兩側及南端均有高聳地形，且重新重飛（go-around）成功的機率極低。據報導，事故發生當時該地區天氣伴隨濃霧，視線受到影響。
目前國家運輸安全委員會已會同聯邦航空總署等相關單位主導事故調查，以釐清航機墜毀的具體原因。調查人員尚未公開殘骸狀況、最終飛行航跡或任何可能存在的機械異常細節，機上全體人員的身分細節亦待官方進一步確認與公布。

en.title: Chartered Cessna 441 Crashes Near Alaska Military Radar Site, Killing 8
en.summary: Security Aviation Cessna 441 crashes near Cape Newenham in Alaska, leaving eight people dead.
body: A chartered Cessna 441 Conquest II turboprop crashed west of Cape Newenham Long Range Radar Site Airport (EHM) in western Alaska at approximately 12:15 local time on August 20, 2026, according to the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA). Emergency rescuers reached the accident scene and confirmed that all eight people on board died in the crash, with no survivors reported.

The twin-engine aircraft, registered as N128EZ and manufactured in 1979, was operated by Anchorage-based Security Aviation. It had departed from Ted Stevens Anchorage International Airport (ANC) carrying two pilots and six passengers. The US Army Corps of Engineers confirmed that it had chartered the flight and that two of its employees were among the fatalities.

The destination airport, located about 450 miles west of Anchorage, is a private US Air Force airstrip servicing a remote radar installation managed by the Pacific Air Forces Regional Support Center. The facility features a single gravel runway, designated Runway 15/33, which measures 3,945 feet long on a mountain slope with an elevation change of over 300 feet.

According to the National Transportation Safety Board (NTSB) Alaska office, the plane crashed while on approach to Cape Newenham. Official FAA airport charts warn of steep surrounding terrain and indicate that successful go-around maneuvers are improbable. Local weather conditions included fog at the time of the accident.

The National Transportation Safety Board (NTSB) is leading the multi-agency investigation into the cause of the fatal crash with direct assistance from the FAA and other federal authorities. Investigators have not yet released public details regarding the wreckage condition, final flight trajectory, or potential mechanical issues, as official coordination remains ongoing.
